title: An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: The standard student edition of Godwin's foundational text of philosophical anarchism, edited by the general editor of the Pickering collected writings, with introduction and notes. It prints the 1793 text alone, so readers needing the 1798 revision or Godwin's other political essays must go to the multi-volume set.

title: The Political and Philosophical Writings of William Godwin (The Pickering Masters, 7 volumes)
author_or_editor: Mark Philp (general editor), with Martin Fitzpatrick and Pamela Clemit
reliability_notes: The scholarly collected edition of Godwin's political, philosophical, educational, literary and religious writings, collated from the editions Godwin himself revised; the novels are not included, and the set was later reissued electronically by Taylor & Francis.

title: An Essay on the Principle of Population: The 1803 Edition (Rethinking the Western Tradition)
reliability_notes: A current scholarly text of Malthus's expanded second essay, the version that shaped nineteenth-century debate, with Stimson's introduction and companion essays; it is a single-edition text rather than the variorum of the 1798 and later editions.

title: Letters and Other Unpublished Writings of Walter Savage Landor
reliability_notes: A Victorian compilation of Landor's correspondence and unpublished papers, still cited for letters not reprinted elsewhere; it is not a complete scholarly edition and later textual work supersedes its readings and attributions.

title: William Cobbett: Selected Writings (The Pickering Masters, 6 volumes)
reliability_notes: The modern scholarly collection of Cobbett's major prose from the years 1792 to 1835, reset and annotated with biographical and analytical introductions, arranged by phase of his career; it is a selection rather than a complete reprint of the Political Register and its pamphlets.

title: Rural Rides (Everyman's Library, 2 volumes)
reliability_notes: The long-standard one-author reading text of Cobbett's survey tours, reprinted from the Political Register serials with Briggs's introduction; it does not attempt a full variorum of the register run and omits most of Cobbett's other polemic.

title: The Journals of Thomas Babington Macaulay (5 volumes)
reliability_notes: The scholarly text of Macaulay's diaries from the later 1820s to 1862, the chief source for his political and literary judgement of his own period; it covers the journals only, not the essays, speeches or correspondence.

title: The Letters of Thomas Babington Macaulay: Volume 2, March 1831-December 1833
reliability_notes: Volume 2 of the definitive Cambridge edition of Macaulay's correspondence, fully annotated and dated from the manuscripts; individual volumes must be cited separately, and the edition stops short of reprinting his published essays and speeches.
